method: kyverno CLI 1.19.2 (cosign-verified release binary) `kyverno apply` of warden-policy/policies/supply-chain/ivp-verify-warden-images.yaml to one Pod using the svc-notify digest, from the operator laptop; -v 6 trace for step timing, GODEBUG=http2debug=2 for every HTTP request
findings: Every registry access re-pings /v2/ and fetches a new anonymous token: 16 token round trips for one image.
The Sigstore trust root (TUF) is initialised once per cosign verification, i.e. 3 times per policy, 6 requests each.
Nothing is reused between the three verifications of the same digest; all ~95 requests are sequential.
At ~0.3 s per round trip this alone explains the 30-36 s; the vulnerability IVP repeats the pattern for its attestation.
implications: The cost is per Pod and per policy, not per release: replicas, restarts and canary steps all pay it.

Levers inside Warden: fewer verifications per Pod (e.g. rely on the signed provenance attestation instead of a separate image signature, needs an ADR), merging the vulnerability check into the same policy, a pinned trusted root instead of TUF, or verifying once per Rollout template.
Levers upstream (Kyverno): reuse the registry token/transport and the TUF client across verifications; cache results per digest.
